ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Symptom relief does not exclude malignancy

A 67-year-old man reports several weeks of new epigastric discomfort, reduced appetite and unintentional weight loss. Famotidine provides partial symptom relief, and he asks to cancel the planned evaluation. Which interpretation of the medication response is most appropriate?

  1. Weight loss is an expected therapeutic effect
  2. Normal symptom control replaces diagnostic assessment
  3. Acid-symptom improvement does not exclude gastric malignancy
  4. Response proves a benign functional disorder
  5. H2 antagonists eliminate early gastric cancer
Answer and explanation

Acid-symptom improvement does not exclude gastric malignancy

The famotidine label cautions that symptom relief does not rule out gastric malignancy; alarm features still require evaluation.

Option explanations

Acid-symptom improvement does not exclude gastric malignancy: The famotidine label cautions that symptom relief does not rule out gastric malignancy; alarm features still require evaluation.

Response proves a benign functional disorder: Benign and malignant conditions can both show symptom improvement.

H2 antagonists eliminate early gastric cancer: H2 blockers are not cancer treatment.

Weight loss is an expected therapeutic effect: Unintentional weight loss is not a desired acid-suppression outcome.

Normal symptom control replaces diagnostic assessment: Clinical assessment is not replaced by treatment response.
